claims.text: The starting catalyst consists of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution particles without additional surface treatment.
Epitaxial deposition of a thin FeCoNi–platinum-group-metal high-entropy-alloy shell will modify the surface electronic structure at the PtPdRhRuIrOs core–shell interface.
The shell-induced electronic modification will reduce catalyst poisoning during ethanol oxidation.
Reduced poisoning will enhance catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
Reduced poisoning and interfacial electronic modification will enhance selectivity during ethanol oxidation.
A well-defined core–shell interface alters the local d-band electronic structure of the catalyst surface.
The high-entropy-alloy shell tunes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates by changing surface electronic states.
Tuned adsorption energies mitigate the accumulation of poisoning species.
Tuned adsorption energies favor reaction pathways that improve ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
Coated catalysts will have a longer operational lifetime and lower deactivation rate than untreated catalysts.
Coated catalysts will produce a higher current density for the desired ethanol-oxidation pathway than untreated catalysts.
Coated catalysts will form fewer unwanted byproducts than untreated catalysts.
The proposed effect should hold only while the shell remains stable under moderate temperatures and pressures typical of standard electrocatalytic setups.
The proposed effect depends on obtaining a uniform, adherent shell without significant interdiffusion at the core–shell interface.
Operando XAS can be used to monitor electronic-state changes at the core–shell interface during ethanol oxidation.
